text: I applied a zero-phase notch filter centered at 50 Hz with a Q-factor of 30 to remove the mains hum from the ECG signal. The zero-phase filtering achieved two passes, providing an attenuation of below -120 dB at the cutoff. Comparing the spectra before and after filtering via FFT, the probe at 50 Hz showed the level dropped from -12 dB to -104 dB (a difference of -92 dB), successfully eliminating the 50 Hz interference while preserving the underlying ECG signal characteristics and reducing the RMS from 0.293 to 0.2336.
